notes.md: - **Kridabhiramamu:** Telugu play by **Vinukonda Vallabharaya** that describes life in **Orugallu (Warangal)**; English edition *A Lover's Guide to Warangal*.

new.s: Which Hoysala king defeated the forces of Yadava Ramachandra in 1305?
new.x: Ballala III (1295–1342) beat Yadava Ramachandra's forces in 1305; he was the last great Hoysala king.
new.angle: U0091 notes gap: Ballala III beat Ramachandra's forces 1305

new.s: In whose reign was the Dnyaneshwari written at Nevasa in 1290?
new.x: Dnyaneshwar wrote the Dnyaneshwari, a Marathi commentary on the Gita, at Nevasa in 1290, in Ramachandra's reign.
new.angle: U0092 notes gap: Dnyaneshwari -> Ramachandra's reign

new.s: Which astronomer was a court scholar of the Yadava ruler Singhana II?
new.x: Singhana II's court had the musician Sarngadeva and the astronomer Changadeva, grandson of Bhaskaracharya.
new.angle: U0092 notes gap: Changadeva, astronomer at Singhana's court

new.s: From which Jain Tirthankara was the Garuda emblem of the early Kakatiyas taken?
new.x: The Garuda emblem came from Tirthankara Shantinatha, whose attendant yaksha is Garuda; it was later replaced by the Varaha.
new.angle: U0093 notes gap: Garuda emblem from Shantinatha

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kakatiya emblem:
1. The Garuda emblem was taken from the Jain Tirthankara Shantinatha.
2. Prola I replaced the Garuda with the Varaha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: Garuda came from Shantinatha's yaksha, and Prola I changed it to Varaha in the Kalyani Chalukya phase.
new.angle: U0093 notes gap: Garuda emblem from Shantinatha

new.s: Who composed the Anumakonda (Thousand Pillar) inscription of Rudradeva?
new.x: The 1163 Anumakonda inscription, which declares Kakatiya independence, was composed by Achitendru.
new.angle: U0093 notes gap: Thousand Pillar inscription composer / finder

new.s: Which scholar found the Anumakonda (Thousand Pillar) inscription of 1163?
new.x: The Thousand Pillar inscription of Rudradeva was found by J.S. Fleet.
new.angle: U0093 notes gap: Thousand Pillar inscription composer / finder

new.s: For which Kalyani Chalukya ruler did Beta I attack Kanchi in 1051?
new.x: Beta I (Garuda Beta) attacked Kanchi in 1051 for his overlord Someshwara I.
new.angle: U0093 notes gap: Beta I attacked Kanchi 1051 for Someshwara I

new.s: Which inscription records the victories of Ambadeva?
new.x: The Tripuranthakam inscription records the victories of Kayastha Ambadeva.
new.angle: U0093 notes gap: Tripuranthakam inscription -> Ambadeva

new.s: The Ramappa temple at Palampet is noted for the use of which material?
new.x: Ramappa, a UNESCO site (2021), stands on a star-shaped platform and is noted for its floating bricks.
new.angle: U0093 notes gap: Ramappa floating bricks

new.s: For control of which regions did Ganapatideva fight the Eastern Gangas?
new.x: Ganapatideva fought the Eastern Gangas for southern Kalinga and Vengi.
new.angle: U0093 notes gap: Ganapatideva vs Eastern Gangas

new.s: Ganapamba, daughter of Ganapatideva, was married to a chief of which family?
new.x: Ganapamba married the Kota chief; Rudrama married the Nidadavolu prince Veerabhadra.
new.angle: U0093 notes gap: Ganapamba married Kota chief

new.s: Ganapatideva's sisters Mailamba and Kundamamba were married to the sons of whom?
new.x: Mailamba and Kundamamba, Ganapatideva's sisters, married sons of Natavadi Buddharaja.
new.angle: U0093 notes gap: sisters married Natavadi Buddharaja's sons

new.s: According to the Bayyaram inscription, who was the progenitor of the Kakatiyas?
new.x: The Bayyaram inscription names Venna Bhupati as progenitor; the Magallu grant names Kakara Gundana.
new.angle: U0093 notes gap: Bayyaram -> Venna Bhupati progenitor

new.s: Who bore the title 'Prithviswara Shirakhandika Kreeda Vinoda'?
new.x: Ganapatideva and Choda Tikka took this title after killing Velanati Prithviswara in 1210.
new.angle: U0093 notes gap: Prithviswara Shirakhandika title

new.s: Which Kakatiya ruler had the longest reign, of 63 years?
new.x: Ganapatideva ruled 1199–1262, about 63 years, the longest Kakatiya reign.
new.angle: U0093 notes gap: longest reign Ganapatideva 63 years

new.s: In June 2026, an ASI survey of which region copied Kakatiya inscriptions among 25 records of the 2nd–16th centuries?
new.x: ASI's Nallamala survey (June 2026) copied Kakatiya inscriptions among 25 records.
new.angle: U0093 notes gap: June 2026 Nallamala ASI survey

new.s: Who was the first woman ruler of the Andhra region?
new.x: Rudrama Devi (1262–1289) was the first woman ruler of the Andhra region.
new.angle: U0094 notes gap: first woman ruler of Andhra

new.s: Rudramma, a daughter of Rudrama Devi, was married to which Yadava prince?
new.x: Rudramma married the Yadava prince Ellanadeva; Mummadamma married Mahadeva and Ruyyamma married Induluri Annaya.
new.angle: U0094 notes gap: Rudrama's sons-in-law

new.s: Who regained Vengi for Rudrama Devi in 1278 by defeating Virabhanudeva?
new.x: Vengi, taken by Ganga Narasimhadeva in 1262, was regained in 1278 when Poti Nayaka and Prolinayaka beat Virabhanudeva.
new.angle: U0094 notes gap: Vengi regained 1278 by Poti and Proli Nayaka

new.s: In which present district is the Chandupatla inscription, which records Rudrama Devi's death, found?
new.x: The Chandupatla inscription is in Nalgonda district; it was set up by her servant Puvvula Mummadi.
new.angle: U0094 notes gap: Chandupatla in Nalgonda district

new.s: What is the name of Marco Polo's travel account?
new.x: The Venetian Marco Polo's work is Il Milione (The Travels).
new.angle: U0094 notes gap: Marco Polo's work Il Milione

new.s: Which survivors of the fall of Warangal led the liberation that produced the Musunuri and Reddi states?
o: Prolaya Nayaka, Racherla Singama and Prolaya Vema
Muppidi Nayaka, Gonavithala and Manuma Gandapalu
new.x: After 1323, Prolaya Nayaka, Racherla Singama and Prolaya Vema led the liberation that gave rise to the Musunuri and Reddi states.
new.angle: U0094 notes gap: liberation leaders -> Musunuri and Reddi states

new.s: Who is the author of the Prataparudra Charitramu?
new.x: Ekamranatha wrote the Prataparudra Charitramu on Kakatiya traditions; Vidyanatha (Agastya) wrote Prataparudra Yashobhushanam.
new.angle: U0094 notes gap: Prataparudra Charitramu -> Ekamranatha

new.s: Who among the following was a court poet of Prataparudra II?
new.x: Sakalya Malla, like Vidyanatha (Agastya), was a court poet of Prataparudra II.
new.angle: U0094 notes gap: Sakalya Malla court poet

new.s: Which work describes the Kakatiya trade route Palnadu–Nalgonda–Nekarikallu–Orugallu?
new.x: Kridabhiramamu names the routes Motupalli–Tripurantakam–Bellary and Palnadu–Nalgonda–Nekarikallu–Orugallu.
new.angle: U0095 notes gap: Kridabhiramamu routes

new.s: According to the Kridabhiramamu, which city was the inland trade hub of the Kakatiya kingdom?
new.x: The Kridabhiramamu routes show Orugallu (Warangal) as the inland trade hub.
new.angle: U0095 notes gap: Kridabhiramamu routes

new.s: How do most scholars describe the nature of the Kakatiya state?
new.x: Most scholars call it a decentralised monarchy; Romila Thapar called it a metropolitan state and Burton Stein compared it to a segmentary state.
new.angle: U0095 notes gap: decentralised monarchy

new.s: Who compiled the Sakala Neeti Sammatamu, a source on Kakatiya administration?
new.x: Sakala Neeti Sammatamu is a 15th-century polity anthology compiled by Madiki Singana.
new.angle: U0095 notes gap: Sakala Neeti Sammatamu -> Madiki Singana

new.s: Who was the Ashwa Sahini (chief of cavalry) of Ganapatideva?
new.x: Gangaya Sahini led Ganapatideva's cavalry; Jayapa was Gaja Sahini and Maraya was Prataparudra II's Ashwa Sahini.
new.angle: U0095 notes gap: Ashwa Sahini Gangaya

new.s: Who were the 'Kolakandru' in the Kakatiya revenue system?
new.x: Kolakandru collected revenue; Arigapulu were the taxpayers.
new.angle: U0095 notes gap: Kolakandru = revenue collectors

new.s: Who was the prime minister of Prataparudra II?
new.x: Muppidi Nayudu was Prataparudra's prime minister; Malyala Hemadri Reddi served Ganapatideva.
new.angle: U0095 notes gap: Muppidi Nayudu PM of Prataparudra

new.s: Who is the author of the Kridabhiramamu?
new.x: Kridabhiramamu, a Telugu play describing life in Orugallu (Warangal), was written by Vinukonda Vallabharaya.
new.angle: U0095 web: Kridabhiramamu author (PYQ y7b1f7c057e7 angle)

new.s: The Kridabhiramamu of Vinukonda Vallabharaya describes life in which city?
new.x: Its English edition is titled 'A Lover's Guide to Warangal': the play is set in Orugallu.
new.angle: U0095 web: Kridabhiramamu describes Orugallu (PYQ y7b1f7c057e7 angle)

new.s: Which inscription records that Visvesvara Sambhu set up a college, a feeding house and a maternity home at Mandadam?
new.x: The Malkapuram inscription (1261) records Visvesvara Sambhu's college, feeding house and prasuti sala at Mandadam.
new.angle: U0096 notes gap: Malkapuram inscription

new.s: Visvesvara Sambhu of the Malkapuram inscription (1261) belonged to which Saiva sect?
new.x: Visvesvara Sambhu of the Golaki matha was a Pasupata Saiva, so the Malkapuram inscription is a key source on that sect.
new.angle: U0096 notes gap: Malkapuram inscription

new.s: Who is called the first Telugu woman poet in her inscriptions?
new.x: Kuppambika, daughter of Gona Budda Reddy and wife of Malyala Gunda, is called the first Telugu woman poet in the Buddapuram inscriptions.
new.angle: U0096 notes gap: Kuppambika first Telugu woman poet

new.s: Which of the following was a Jain centre in the Kakatiya period?
new.x: Kolanupaka was a Jain centre, with Bodhan, Vemulawada and Patancheru; the others were Shaiva centres.
new.angle: U0096 notes gap: Jain centres (Kolanupaka)

new.s: Who built the Padmakshi temple at Hanumakonda, originally a Jain shrine?
new.x: The Padmakshi temple at Hanumakonda was built by Prola II and was first a Jain shrine.
new.angle: U0096 notes gap: Padmakshi temple built by Prola II

new.s: Who spread Veerashaivism in Andhra?
new.x: Palkuriki Somanatha spread Veerashaivism in Andhra, drawing artisans and lower groups into it.
new.angle: U0096 notes gap: Palkuriki Somanatha spread Veerashaivism
